record.paper_title: Heavy flavors and quarkonia: highlights, open questions, and perspectives
record.original_question: For charm-strange resonances with lifetimes comparable to the 5–10 fm/c hadron-gas phase between chemical and kinetic freeze-out, does the D*s2+(2573)/Ds+ yield ratio truly decrease with charged-particle multiplicity, and if so, how does that multiplicity dependence reveal the interplay between resonance lifetime and hadronic rescattering that suppresses reconstructable resonance yields?

evidence.quote: The hadron-gas phase lasts approximately 5-10 fm/c from the chemical freeze-out, right after the hadronisation of the QGP, to the kinetic freeze-out, when all interactions cease and hadrons stream freely.
As a consequence, the measured resonance yield is suppressed with respect to the amount produced at the chemical freeze-out.
While no clear multiplicity dependence is observed for the D+s1(2536)/D+s ratio, the D*s2+(2573)/D+s result shows a hint of decreasing trend (left panel of Fig. 5), though with large uncertainties.

If confirmed by more precise measurements, such results might shed light on the interplay between the different hadron lifetimes and the hadronic rescattering, which is expected to influence their abundance.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider high-energy hadronic collisions (e.g., pp, p–Pb, or Pb–Pb at LHC energies) in which a quark–gluon plasma is produced and subsequently hadronizes at chemical freeze-out, followed by a hadron-gas phase of typical duration 5–10 fm/c that ends at kinetic freeze-out, when all interactions cease. During the hadron-gas phase, hadronic resonances with proper lifetimes comparable to this duration may either decay inside the medium (so that their decay products undergo rescattering and the parent cannot be reconstructed) or regenerate via pseudoelastic interactions of their decay products, leading to a multiplicity-dependent modification of the reconstructable resonance yield.

Focus on the two open-charm-strange resonances D_{s1}(2536)^+ and D*_{s2}(2573)^+, and let their yields be normalized to the prompt D_s^+ meson yield in the same event class. Let dN_ch/dη denote the average charged-particle pseudorapidity density characterizing event multiplicity.

Establish the following:

(a) Determine whether the yield ratio D*_{s2}(2573)^+ / D_s^+ exhibits a statistically significant monotonically decreasing trend as a function of dN_ch/dη.

(b) Determine whether the yield ratio D_{s1}(2536)^+ / D_s^+ remains independent of dN_ch/dη within uncertainties.

(c) Quantitatively relate any observed multiplicity dependence of these ratios to the resonance proper lifetimes and to a model of hadronic rescattering and regeneration in the hadron-gas phase, thereby exposing how the interplay between resonance lifetime and hadronic-phase dynamics suppresses (or preserves) reconstructable resonance yields with increasing multiplicity.
artifact.category_tag: Heavy-flavor resonance production in heavy-ion collisions
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate that hadronic rescattering effects have been quantitatively established for light-flavor resonances (e.g., K*(892)^0, ρ(770)^0) and shown to depend mainly on produced charged-particle multiplicity, but for the charm-strange resonances D_{s1}(2536)^+ and D*_{s2}(2573)^+ only a hint of a decreasing D*_{s2}/D_s^+ trend with large uncertainties has been reported, with no precise confirmation. Thus the specific question for charm-strange resonances remains open.

status_evidence.title: System size dependence of the hadronic rescattering effect at LHC energies
status_evidence.snippet: The hadronic rescattering effect is found to be independent of the size of colliding systems and mainly driven by the produced charged-particle multiplicity (results focused on light-flavor resonances).
status_evidence.claim: Rescattering effect quantified for light-flavor resonances, not charm-strange.

status_evidence.title: Exploring hadronic rescattering effects on resonance productions
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses hadronic rescattering effects on resonance productions; charm-strange resonance measurements still limited in precision.
status_evidence.claim: Charm-strange resonance multiplicity dependence not conclusively established.
